page: Amazon Web Services g6.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It integrates an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7R13 processor running at 3.4 GHz with 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs, paired with 256 GB of DDR4 system memory clocked at 3 GHz. Acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA L4 Tensor Core GPU from the Ada Lovelace architecture, equipped with 22 GB of total VRAM. The instance also provisions 1880 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and delivers a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing capabilities across both CPU and GPU execution paths. Multi-core performance is ranked in the top 25 percent in stress-ng (95679.04), Geekbench multi-core (16623.0), and PassMark CPU tests (60669.57), backed by high scores in software compilation and cryptographic routines. In-memory data structures exhibit high throughput, reflected in 62.3 million Redis SET operations per second. For artificial intelligence tasks, the NVIDIA L4 GPU delivers top-tier performance on small (135M) and medium (7B) language models for both prompt ingestion and token generation. However, larger 70B parameter models encounter physical memory constraints on the 22 GB GPU, dropping text generation rates into the bottom 25 percent.

Resource allocation delivers a balanced 4 GB of RAM per vCPU alongside fast local NVMe storage, making it cost-efficient for single-GPU acceleration pipelines that require significant auxiliary host computing and memory. Workloads best suited for this instance include medium-scale AI inference, video transcoding, graphics workstation rendering, ray tracing, and high-concurrency microservices paired with local caching.
description: Amazon Web Services g6.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 64 vCPUs, 256 GB of DDR4 memory, and a single NVIDIA L4 GPU with 22 GB of VRAM. Built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture, it incorporates 1880 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system excels in multi-threaded computation, software compilation, and in-memory operations, demonstrating top-tier throughput in Redis benchmarks and small-to-medium large language model inference. Performance scales effectively for models up to 7B parameters, though larger 70B models show constrained token generation speeds due to single-card VRAM limits. This configuration provides a high-density compute, storage, and graphics profile suited for real-time AI inference, ray tracing, video processing, and concurrent web backends.
